definitions.explanation: The polite form of {名前|なまえ} (name), formed by adding the honorific prefix お. Used when asking about or referring to someone else's name in polite or formal situations.

examples.japanese: お{名前|なまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧お⟦{聞|き}かせ→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦いただけます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Could you tell me your name?

examples.japanese: ⟦こちら→こちら：00960_kochira⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{名前|なまえ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{住所|じゅうしょ}→住所：01430_juusho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ご⟦{記入|きにゅう}→記入：02624_kinyuu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please write your name and address here.

notes:
One of the first polite expressions learners encounter. The お prefix makes ⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧ honorific, so it is used to refer to the listener's or a third person's name, not one's own.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{名前|なまえ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧？ — What is your name? (casual-polite)
- お{名前|なまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{伺|うかが}って⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦よろしい→よろしい：01176_yoroshii⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ — May I ask your name? (very polite)
- お{名前|なまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦どうぞ→どうぞ：02920_douzo⟧ — Your name, please

USAGE:
- At receptions, clinics, and service counters, staff will say お{名前|なまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧お⟦{願|ねが}い→願い：03529_negai⟧します (your name, please)
- When filling out forms, instructions may say お{名前|なまえ} to indicate the name field
- Do not use お{名前|なまえ} when giving your own name; simply say ⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧ or ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧～です
